items.statement: Fundraise is under process to support capex, working capital for B2G and export orders, and debt reduction.
items.quote: And there are multiple assets which are not -- which would be of no use once we have shifted. So all these would be adding on to it. There would be multiple additions and as well as we are doing some fundraise, which is under process right now.

items.statement: Loans and guarantees limit raised to INR300 crores from INR100 crores as a precautionary measure, not for distribution to friends or relatives.
items.quote: No, this was just to be on the safe side. It was not done with the intention of definitely not distributing anything to the friends and relatives, but it was done mainly to increase -- we were at INR100 crores earlier and we just went on to do it up to INR300 crores, but then there was no such intent behind doing this.

items.statement: Receivables over 3 years of INR10.26 crores are largely due to a 90-120 day billing cycle cut-off issue; provisions taken for unrecoverable amounts.
items.quote: So, it's not like the whole amount is sitting there since 3 years, but it's more or less the balance that remains unpaid at the end of a particular reporting period. But yes, we have been putting some thought into the amount that we are not able to recover. And there is some provision also that has been taken if you see, so that we are covered for the receivables that we think are not recoverable

items.statement: Loans and advances of INR48 crores are advance payments to vendors due to working capital intensive nature; they scale with revenue and are recoverable.
items.quote: Those are basically advances for, you know, the advances part is the advances for the expenses that we incur. So, we have explained it in -- earlier also, I think that we are a very capital, working capital intensive business.

items.statement: No dilution planned for FY26 or FY27; current cash and bank balance sufficient for planned operations and capex.
items.quote: No. As of now, we are not planning it. Yes. As of now, it's not in the works.

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved and non-core assets monetized to manage debt levels
items.quote: And at the same time, I think with an improved operating cash flow situation and also in the recent past, we have monetize d some non -core

items.statement: Management is considering a fundraise via equity (widespread) for the INR 100 crore hospitality CAPEX, not debt.
items.quote: We are considering some sort of widespread is our initial thought, but it's early days. We are looking to do it via equity and not by debt.

items.statement: Management says working capital is sufficient and no additional working capital is needed until FY27 even with 25% growth
items.quote: I think Working capital is sufficient. Till the next financial year, in 26-27 also, we don't ne ed additional working capital

items.statement: Management states Barota Finance AUM was around 130 crore last year and targets 150-160 crore for FY27
items.quote: Last... last year, our AUM was around 130 odd crores. And maybe, , we can look for a target of around 150 to 160 crores.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased to around Rs. 68 crores
items.quote: Because I was asking this question because the trade receivable increased to around Rs. 68 crores, if I'm right. Piyush Garodia: Yes.

items.statement: Promoter holding remains low due to past preferential allotments where management did not participate; recent preferential allotment maintained current stake level with no near-term plan to increase.
items.quote: We recently had a small preferential, allotment as well, but their promoters have also taken an equivalent amount to their current holdings. So the stake is likely to remain this level.

items.statement: Working capital cycle is best in industry with CC limit of only 3-4 crores on ~150 crore business; sales converted via customer bill discounting and tight inventory management.
items.quote: even with a, you know, a business of about 150 crores. We have a working capital CC limit of just about 3-4 crores, you know, which, typically for any other company would be, you know, anywhere between 20-25 crores.

items.statement: Rights issue of INR 49.5 crore for a 4 MW solar project; promoters taking full quota and possibly more
items.quote: This rights issue is 49.5 crore level. And promoters, we are taking almost like our entire quota. Maybe we'll be taking a little more also.

items.statement: Working capital deployed from IPO proceeds; monthly billing on funded government projects with no payment risk but high working capital needs
items.quote: So, as I have already said that we have already deployed most of the working capital from the IPO and in the sense of receivables, there is a billing every month in every government project.

items.statement: Retention money increased to 5% in NBCC projects, some retention not releasable against bank guarantee, creating working capital hold
items.quote: Yes, retention money. Ealier in CPWD, they were having a 2.5% retention money, but now most of the projects like we are doing is NBCC and alL. So, they have a 5% retention money

items.statement: Preferential warrant proceeds will fund acquisition of a non-India company or physical presence in North America, Europe or Australia
items.quote: And that's what we came out with our preferential warrant, where those money will be utilizing for acquiring a local non-India based company, mainly into North America or Europe or in Australia, but mainly in North America.

items.statement: Plans to invest Rs 12-18 crore over next 12-24 months on AI, blockchain and cybersecurity R&D and centre of excellence
items.quote: So, all in all, around 12 crores to 18 crores is what we are expecting to invest for R&D or for a center of excellence creation.
